name: bell-operations
title: A Bell-pair circuit becomes timed physical operations
caption: The circuit is an ideal interface. A physical implementation must specify the encoded levels, reset, drive, interaction, and measurement. Time runs left to right.

name: level-selectivity
title: Energy spacing determines spectral selectivity
caption: The spacings, not just the existence of two selected states, determine whether a drive can address the qubit without exciting higher levels. Level positions are schematic.

name: echo-sign
title: Echo reverses the sign of a static frequency error
caption: The sign refers to the frequency term in a toggling frame. Echo refocuses a constant offset; it neither reverses relaxation nor cancels arbitrary rapidly varying noise.

name: josephson-circuit
title: A nonlinear circuit and its selected levels
caption: The capacitor stores charge energy and the Josephson junction supplies −EJ cos φ. The small ladder is schematic; the chapter derives its approximate transition spacings.

name: ion-sidebands
title: Internal transitions can change shared motion
caption: The carrier connects equal motional occupation; the red sideband changes |0,n⟩ to |1,n−1⟩ in the stated drive convention. The separated ladders suppress the large internal energy offset for readability.

name: rydberg-pair
title: Blockade shifts the double excitation
caption: The added energy of |rr⟩ changes the resonance condition for the second excitation. The levels and arrows are schematic; a full gate also needs pulse phases and local corrections.

name: double-dot
title: Two confined spins and a tunable barrier
caption: The orbital confinement and spin splitting are different energy scales. Exchange depends on wavefunction overlap across the barrier; physical dot positions alone do not specify the gate.

name: defect-levels
title: A selected transition in a spin-one defect
caption: Selecting two levels does not remove the third. The displayed frequencies follow from D Sz² + γe B Sz; strain, transverse fields, and optical levels require a fuller model.

name: photonic-interferometer
title: Path phase becomes an output probability
caption: The two horizontal lines are optical modes, not two photons. A single photon occupies a coherent superposition of paths. The probability formulas use the real beam-splitter convention stated in the text.

name: binomial-loss
title: One loss changes parity without reading this code
caption: The drawn arrows describe the lowering operator acting on the codewords, not deterministic recovery. Both logical alternatives have mean occupation two. No-jump evolution and higher-order errors still require analysis.

name: majorana-exchange
title: An ideal exchange is a path through configuration space
caption: Time runs downward. Dashed and solid trajectories distinguish the two exchanged modes; the stationary third mode shows why a subsequent neighboring exchange can have order-dependent action. This is an ideal braid diagram, not evidence for a device.

name: feedback-pipeline
title: Feedback latency and throughput are different
caption: Rectangles represent classical acquisition and processing intervals. Overlap shows pipelining, not instantaneous feedback. The times are schematic; a dependent gate must still wait for its result.

name: routing-graph
title: A physical interaction graph constrains routing
caption: The dashed curve is the requested operation, not a native interaction. For endpoints at distance three, the explicit move-and-restore strategy uses four SWAPs. Other compilers may retain a changed placement.

name: parity-extraction
title: Measure joint parity using one auxiliary
caption: The ideal circuit preserves coherence within each parity sector. Two data wires and one auxiliary wire are shown; gate faults and repeated noisy measurements require a separate analysis.

name: repetition-error
title: Redundancy helps only for a specified noise model
caption: Perfect majority decoding gives 3p²−2p³ under independent bit flips. This encoding does not protect arbitrary phase errors.

name: detuning-bound
title: A detuning suppresses an isolated unwanted transition
caption: The isolated constant-drive bound is 1/[1+(Δ/Ω)²]. It is not a complete multilevel leakage prediction.

name: rabi-detuning
title: Detuning changes both frequency and oscillation height
caption: All traces start in zero under the constant-drive two-state model. Resonance reaches full inversion; detuning imposes a ceiling that changing duration cannot remove.

name: pulse-spectrum
title: A rectangular pulse has spectral sidelobes
caption: The curve is sinc²(ΔT/2), normalized to its zero-detuning value. It describes a Fourier-weight estimate in weak excitation, not an exact resonant π-pulse probability.

name: exchange-populations
title: Exchange transfers one excitation coherently
caption: Under H/ℏ = g(XX+YY)/2, the 01 and 10 populations follow cos²(gt) and sin²(gt). Equal populations at gt=π/4 accompany the relative phase −i stated in the text.

name: mediator-overlap
title: A residual mediator record lowers data coherence
caption: The curve exp(−|Δα|²/2) is the magnitude of the coherent-state overlap. Correct data populations can coexist with this loss of phase-sensitive contrast.

name: readout-signals
title: Overlapping signals require a decision rule
caption: Equal-variance Gaussian models are centered two standard deviations apart. Their overlap causes assignment errors. A midpoint threshold is optimal here only for equally likely preparations and symmetric decision costs.

name: thermal-preparation
title: The energy-to-temperature ratio controls thermal excitation
caption: The normalized two-level Boltzmann population is 1/(1+exp[ℏω/kBT]). This assumes equilibrium of the qubit, not simply a stated refrigerator temperature.

name: relaxation-coherence
title: Population and coherence have different decay rates
caption: The relaxation-only coherence envelope is exp(−t/2T₁). Adding independent exponential pure dephasing at Tφ = 100 μs gives T₂ = 66.7 μs. These are model curves, not measured traces.

name: ramsey-fringes
title: A Ramsey trace separates fringe frequency from contrast
caption: The illustrative trace has period 2 μs, visibility 0.9, and an assumed exponential envelope. A cosine-only period gives detuning magnitude, not its sign.

name: benchmark-decay
title: A sequence-length decay is a model-dependent inference
caption: Both curves use A = 0.45 and B = 0.5. Under the effective single-qubit depolarizing model, infidelity per fitted element is (1−α)/2; it is not automatically per native pulse.

name: transmon-spectrum
title: A weakly anharmonic transmon ladder
caption: Quartic-approximation levels use EJ/h = 20 GHz and EC/h = 0.25 GHz. Neighboring gaps decrease by about 0.25 GHz. The plot is a low-level approximation, not an exact or measured spectrum.

name: motion-closure
title: A single-mode force closes its displacement
caption: For g/δ = 0.25, α = (g/δ)(1−exp[iδt]) returns to zero at δt = 2π. This closure removes the ideal mediator displacement while an S² phase remains. Other modes and heating are omitted.

name: blockade-suppression
title: An isolated blockade estimate improves with |B|/Ω
caption: At |B|/Ω = 20 the bound is 1/401. It excludes Rydberg decay, pulse phase error, motion, and multilevel structure; it is not a total gate infidelity.

name: spin-exchange
title: A Heisenberg exchange pulse sets the SWAP time
caption: The stated exchange-energy convention gives SWAP at 50 ns and an equal-weight entangling state at 25 ns. This differs from the angular-frequency g convention in Chapter 4.

name: collection-rate
title: Two required photons make efficiency a quadratic resource
caption: This two-photon toy rate assumes independent detection and accepted-pattern factor q = 1/2. Conditional state quality also depends on mode overlap and false detections.

name: hong-ou-mandel
title: Wavepacket overlap suppresses coincidences
caption: For the assumed squared overlap |μ|² = exp[−(delay/τ)²], the ideal probability is (1−|μ|²)/2. This is an analytical overlap model, not a fitted experimental dip.

name: finite-grid
title: Finite-width peaks illustrate a grid encoding
caption: The schematic density uses even multiples of √π, finite peak width, and a finite envelope. It is not an ideal infinite-energy codeword and does not by itself show the required momentum protection.

name: finite-size-splitting
title: A conditional finite-size model suppresses splitting
caption: The exponential is an illustrative finite-size model; real systems can include oscillations and other terms. Reduced splitting alone does not establish protected operations or suppress nonequilibrium parity changes.

name: cold-stage-budget
title: Other heat loads reduce the line-count budget
caption: All quantities refer to the same hypothetical temperature stage. The line-only bound is 500; a 4 μW fixed load reduces it to 300. This is accounting, not a refrigerator specification.

name: link-wait
title: Retries convert per-attempt success into waiting probability
caption: The curves are 1−(1−s)^N. Mean attempts are 1/s, while the distribution has a long tail that affects memory waiting and multi-link scheduling.

name: logical-fit
title: A logical-error fit must name its physical regime
caption: The illustrative fit A(p/pth)^((d+1)/2), with A = 0.1, improves with distance only below its assumed threshold. It is not a universal theorem or a prediction from one average gate fidelity.

name: zero-failure-bound
title: Zero observed failures still leaves statistical uncertainty
caption: The bound follows by solving (1−q)^N = 0.05 for q when no failures are seen. Independent identical trials are assumed; drift and systematic bias are not included.

name: accepted-rate
title: Compare useful output rates with acceptance included
caption: The illustrative rate is s/τ before calibration overhead. Faster accepted output does not establish adequate state quality; the output error target must also be met.
